$description: ALYR design tokens: the one source for every colour, face, size, space, radius, rule, motion value, breakpoint and focus style ALYR shows. Carbon and Volt (D-040). Edit this file, then run `node scripts/tokens-build.mjs`; never edit the generated files. Format: DTCG-style (see design/README.md for where it departs from the 2025.10 format).

color.$description: Primitives. Every literal colour is named once, here. Code never uses these names directly: it uses the semantic and component tokens below, which point at them.

carbon.$description: Carbon. The command surface, the logo, the main ink.

volt.$description: Volt. A signal only: the main action, the current state, confirmed progress, one strategic highlight. Never body text on a light surface, never a decorative background.

volt-hover.$description: Volt under the pointer: a step darker.

volt-pressed.$description: Volt while pressed: two steps darker.

concrete.$description: Concrete. Muted text in dark mode and on Carbon.

graphite.$description: Graphite. Lines in dark mode; the selected tab on Carbon.

ink.$description: Brand colours that are never used on their own as a surface.

chalk.$description: Text in dark mode and on Carbon.

volt-ink.$description: Volt as text on a light surface (6.4:1 on white), where Volt itself would not read.

on-volt.$description: Text and icons on a Volt fill.

moss.$description: The light theme's focus ring: Volt's family, dark enough to see on Paper.

grey.$description: One neutral ramp. Each step is named by its CIELAB lightness times ten (grey-873 is L* 87.3), so a new step slots in without renaming. Carbon, Paper, Chalk, Concrete and Graphite keep their brand names and are not repeated here. Steps marked 'retire' are used by one drawing or the report card only, kept so those stay exactly as published.

485.$description: Marks on Carbon: idle dots, dashed rules, small outlined buttons.

445.$description: Faint ink in the light drawings (retire: drawings only).

428.$description: Muted text, light (5.6:1 on Paper). Line strong, dark.

264.$description: The drawn phone's outline. The drawn document's labels in dark mode.

260.$description: The Carbon report card's ghost bars.

169.$description: The workspace window drawn on a dark page.

154.$description: A panel inside a Carbon block, dark mode.

140.$description: A subtle surface inside a Carbon block.

121.$description: Carbon blocks in dark mode, lifted a step off the dark canvas.

106.$description: Raised row in the dark drawings (retire: drawings only).

101.$description: A panel inside a Carbon block, light mode.

067.$description: Card in the dark drawings (retire: drawings only).

050.$description: The drawn workspace chat, dark (retire: drawings only).

033.$description: The drawn phone's bezel, light (retire: drawings only).

030.$description: Background of the dark drawings (retire: drawings only).

014.$description: The drawn phone's frame on the ALYR Chat page.

status.$description: Status hues, product only. The brand has no status colours on the public site.

drawing.$description: Colours only the drawn product screens on the site use.

sent.$description: A sent message in the drawn workspace chat.

whatsapp.$description: WhatsApp's own chat colours, for drawn chats only. They are WhatsApp's, not ALYR's: never use them for anything else, and never with WhatsApp's logo.

soft-sent.$description: ALYR's shade: WhatsApp's grey is 4.2:1 on a sent bubble; this keeps 4.5:1.

rule.$description: Rules in light; text in dark.

brand-green.$description: WhatsApp's brand green. Only the customer pages' small 'back to WhatsApp' disc uses it; the public site never does.

soft-sent-dark.$description: ALYR's shade, lighter than WhatsApp's, to keep 4.5:1.

shop.$description: A shop's own colour, chosen on the sales demo's setup panel (/demo/bakery, ALY-263). They are the shop's, never ALYR's: only on the shop's own marks (its monogram, its order page bar, its map pin, its QR card) inside drawings. Each carries white text at 4.5:1 or better.

semantic.$description: The API. Every page and screen reads these names; each has a light value and, where it changes, a dark one ($extensions qa.alyr.dark).

surface.$description: A sheet or panel on the canvas.

surface-subtle.$description: A step off the surface: a raised row, a well, a hover.

text-muted.$description: 4.5:1 or better on canvas and surface in both themes.

text-faint.$description: Labels and metadata only, never a sentence (3:1).

line-strong.$description: 3:1 for controls and marks that must be seen. Darker than the design system's strong border, which is 2.1:1 on Paper.

hair.$description: A hairline that takes the colour under it.

volt-ink.$description: Volt as text: the dark green on light, Volt itself on dark.

volt-wash.$description: Pale Volt behind the current row.

pending.$description: The hollow dot for something not yet available. Never an error.

white.$description: White that stays white in dark mode: a switch's knob, text on a status fill.

black.$description: Masks and the darkest shadows only.

component.$description: Tokens that belong to one component. They point at the semantic or primitive tokens; a literal here is a value nothing else uses.

band.$description: Carbon blocks: the band, the hero plate, the closing call, the product page opening. Carbon in both themes, lifted a step in dark so it stands off the dark canvas. What sits inside keeps its place: wells under it, panels over it.

band-edge.$description: The hairline that closes a full-bleed Carbon section (dark only).

dark-canvas.$description: A well inside a Carbon block.

dark-surface.$description: A panel inside a Carbon block.

on-band.$description: Headings, names and current items on Carbon.

on-band-faint.$description: Notes and idle steps on Carbon.

band-mark.$description: Idle dots, dashed rows and outlined small buttons on Carbon.

band-rule.$description: Dashed wires, separators and underlines on Carbon.

window.$description: A window of the workspace drawn on a page, and the numbered marks beside a figure.

mark-ring.$description: Numbered marks are Carbon discs, ringed in Volt only in dark.

monogram-bg.$description: A shop's monogram tile, Carbon in both themes.

theme-switch.$description: Which theme is showing, as numbers and display values, so the switch needs no rules of its own per theme.

chat.$description: The drawn WhatsApp chat (the ALYR Chat page, the report phone, onboarding's preview): WhatsApp's own light and dark chat screens, no logo.

drawing.$description: The product's screens drawn on the public site (drawings.css). They copy the customer pages and the workspace as they were when drawn; the product has since moved to the semantic surfaces (D-040), so the drawn surfaces are due to follow in a change the founder sees first.

grid.$description: The construction grid behind the homepage hero.

document.$description: A receipt or invoice drawn on the site (_site/paper.css): the paper, its ink, its rules and its totals band. Paper stays paper in dark mode: turned down a step, never inverted, so the document still reads as the thing a customer holds. Ink and ink-2 keep 4.5:1 or better on the paper in both themes.

paper.$description: In dark mode a step below the brightest grey, so a full A4 does not glare on the dark canvas.

ink-2.$description: Labels and the English twin of each Arabic line: 5.8:1 on white, 7.7:1 on the dark theme's paper, 6.5:1 on its band.

rule.$description: Rules and dashed separators inside the paper only.

band.$description: The table head and the totals band.

agent.$description: ALYR Agent's dashboard (agent.css) maps its --ag-* hooks onto the semantic tokens; only the bar and ghost mixes change with the theme.

bar-mix.$description: How much ink the week's bars carry.

ghost-mix.$description: How much ink last week's ghost bars carry.

card.$description: The Sunday report card (apps/api/src/alyr/modules/agent/card.py), 1080 x 566, in two themes. Read from Python and TypeScript; not emitted to CSS.

carbon.$description: The default: reads in a light and a dark chat alike.

email.$description: The sign-in and weekly report emails (core/mail.py, modules/report.py). Light only for now. Read from Python; not emitted to CSS.

social.$description: The social card (socialCard.tsx), 1200 x 630, Carbon only. Read from TypeScript.

shop.$description: The sales demo's shop colours (/demo/bakery): the shop's own brand on its monogram, order page bar, map pin and QR card, picked on the setup panel. The same in both themes; white text on each is 4.5:1 or better. Never ALYR's accent, never a surface.

ink.$description: Text and marks on a shop colour.

family.$description: The first name in each of sans, arabic and mono is the face itself. On the web every brand face is replaced by the variable next/font sets for it (qa.alyr.nextFont), because next/font self-hosts the face under a hashed name.

arabic.$description: Arabic. Never letter-spaced; looser line height than Latin.

ui.$description: Product screens and the Agent: Latin first, Arabic for any Arabic in it.

ui-arabic.$description: Product screens and the Agent in Arabic.

chat.$description: The drawn WhatsApp chat: the phone's own system face, as WhatsApp uses it.

ui-mono.$description: Labels in product screens and the Agent.

email.$description: Email clients do not load web fonts reliably.

file.$description: The font files images are rendered with (the report card in apps/api, the social card in apps/web), SIL Open Font Licence.

weight.$description: Instrument Sans is variable; the site uses its in-between weights. Product screens, the Agent and the card use 400, 500 and 600 only.

site.$description: The public site: fluid headings, rem steps. Arabic uses the same sizes with its own line heights.

ui.$description: Product screens and the Agent: a fixed px scale for dense screens. 16 px is for inputs (a phone zooms into anything smaller).

stage.$description: The sales demo (/demo/bakery, ALY-263): one idea per screen on a laptop at arm's length, 1024 to 1440 px wide and more. Larger than the site's display on purpose; nothing else uses them.

hero.$description: The one line a scene opens on.

title.$description: A scene's heading beside a figure.

lead.$description: The line under a heading, and card text.

card.$description: The report card's 1080 px canvas. Nothing smaller than 31 px (about 9.5 px on a phone).

tracking.$description: Latin only. Arabic is never tracked and never set in capitals.

space.$description: 8 px steps (4 for the tightest gaps). Sections and the gutter are fluid.

sec.$description: Padding above and below a section.

radius.$description: Controls are nearly square; the 45-degree cut, not a radius, is the brand's shape.

border.$description: A solid rule is true today; a dashed rule is a slot waiting to become true.

dashed.$description: Followed by a colour: line-strong on the page, band-rule on Carbon.

cut.$description: The 45-degree cut from the logo's diagonal. Mirrored in Arabic: clip-path does not flip.

plate-sm.$description: The hero plate's corner on phones.

fold-gap.$description: The Paper gaps through the fold.

lift.$description: A sheet resting on the canvas.

float.$description: A menu or sheet above the page.

motion.$description: One signature gesture: things arrive along the logo's 45-degree diagonal, settle, and one Volt signal confirms them. Everything plays once, except what follows the scroll.

fast.$description: The site's older scale, still in use; fold into dur-* as pages are touched.

pace.$description: The pace of every timed piece on the site: the flows, the demos, the signature figures, the products frame's tiles, the business day's fold, the X-ray, the reveals and the heading splits. The interaction scale above (hovers, presses, menus, the theme switch, the product screens) does not change with it. Every value here is multiplied by `pace` (CSS `calc(… * var(--pace))`, TypeScript and Python already multiplied), so one number tunes them all. Founder, 25 Oct 2026: the timed pieces were too slow; this group made them about 40% quicker.

The one setting. 1 was the pace chosen on 25 Oct 2026; the founder found it too fast on 26 Oct, so 1.3 (30% slower than that, still about 22% quicker than before the pace). Lower is quicker (0.8 is 20% quicker), higher is slower (1.25 is 25% slower). The play-* durations, the play stagger and the dwell's reading time and beat follow it; dwell-min does not, so a step is never shorter than it.

play-1.$description: A timed piece's shortest move: a hold, a swap of two words. 0.6 of dur-1.

play-2.$description: A tick, a press, a small fade inside a timed piece. 0.6 of dur-2.

play-3.$description: A message, a row or a line arriving inside a timed piece. 0.6 of dur-3.

play-4.$description: A panel, a paper or a section arriving; the longest single move. 0.6 of dur-4.

play-stagger.$description: The beat of a timed piece: every delay inside one is a number of these. 0.6 of stagger.

read-word.$description: Time to read one word at 230 words a minute. A step of a flow or a tab of a demo dwells for its words times this, plus dwell-beat.

dwell-beat.$description: The short beat after a step's words are read, before the next step.

dwell-min.$description: No step or tab dwells for less, whatever the pace.

live-beat.$description: The live ALYR Agent figure (D-058): one product event every this long on a wide screen (5.2 s at pace 1.3). Paced since 26 Oct 2026, so the founder's 'a bit slower' reaches the hero too.

live-beat-phone.$description: The same beat on a phone, where the motion stays lighter (6.5 s at pace 1.3).

ease-fold.$description: A cover that should be seen crossing: the sales demo's 45° scene fold (/demo/bakery, ALY-263), an even sweep in and out. Not for things arriving.

ease-product.$description: The product screens' curve until they move to --ease.

spring-product.$description: The product screens' spring until they move to --spring.

travel.$description: How far things travel along 45 degrees.

breakpoint.$description: Media queries cannot read custom properties, so these are written in CSS as numbers; this list says which ones exist. The product's own (720, 860, 1100 px; 40 and 56 rem) are not on it yet.

tablet.$description: 768 px: the Agent's container query too.

contact-bar.$description: Below this the sticky contact bar shows.

focus.$description: A 2 px ring in --focus (moss on light, Volt on dark and on Carbon), 2 px off the element, 3 px off a button.
